# Gstarcademy - Full Knowledge Graph & Terminology Index

This document contains all core terminology, definitions, and application contexts curated on Gstarcademy. It is designed for LLMs to build semantic memory of our CAD/BIM knowledge base.

## Core Glossary Terms

### Layer
- **Tags**: terms beginner 2d
- **Definition**: A logical container controlling visibility, color, line type, and plotting behavior.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Start with layers to keep drawings readable and editable.

### Block
- **Tags**: terms beginner 2d
- **Definition**: Reusable grouped geometry, often used for symbols and repeated components.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Blocks reduce repetitive drafting work and improve consistency.

### Xref
- **Tags**: terms beginner aec
- **Definition**: External reference file linked into a drawing for collaboration across teams.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Critical in AEC multi‑discipline projects.

### Constraint
- **Tags**: terms 3d beginner
- **Definition**: Rules in sketch/model that lock geometry relationships and design intent.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Key to parametric modeling behavior.

### Tolerance
- **Tags**: terms standards collaboration
- **Definition**: Allowed dimensional variation for manufacturing and assembly acceptance.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Fundamental term for mechanical production quality.

### BIM
- **Tags**: terms aec 3d
- **Definition**: Building Information Modeling: data‑rich model approach for AEC lifecycle workflows.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Not only geometry, also metadata and coordination.

### DWG compatibility mode
- **Tags**: terms 2d mfg
- **Definition**: How a CAD platform reads/writes Autodesk‑style DWGs—fonts, substitutes, proxies, scale lists.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Consult your exact build’s migration chapter; never assume bit‑for‑bit identity across vendors.

### Command alias (PGP)
- **Tags**: terms 2d mfg
- **Definition**: Keyboard shortcuts to commands—the muscle memory bridge when moving between DWG editors.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Aliases differ by platform; keep a personal table when you multi‑boot Linux/Windows.

### Mechanical BOM
- **Tags**: terms mfg
- **Definition**: Bill of materials generated from parts lists in mechanical verticals—ties annotations to rows and quantity fields.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Validate against your PDM/ERP export template before production cutover.

### Point cloud (scan)
- **Tags**: terms 3d
- **Definition**: Dense 3D measurement points from LiDAR/photogrammetry used for as‑builts and clash context.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Registration, noise, and density drive whether you trace linework or model directly.

### AEC object style
- **Tags**: terms aec
- **Definition**: Wall/slab/stair styles in architectural verticals—parameters drive plan/elevation behavior like a lightweight BIM‑lite.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Export expectations to plain DWG may flatten smart objects—plan your deliverable early.

### SYSVAR
- **Tags**: terms beginner
- **Definition**: System variables controlling snaps, file paths, user preferences—think global toggles with saved profiles.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Back up a known‑good profile before experimenting in production projects.

### PDF underlay
- **Tags**: terms 2d
- **Definition**: Attach a PDF page behind vector geometry for tracing or redlines without converting every entity.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Watch scale and layer contrast; heavy PDFs can slow pan/zoom.

### GRX / .NET API
- **Tags**: terms mfg
- **Definition**: Vendor APIs to automate commands, build add‑ins, or integrate data—differs from simple script macros.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Match API level to your build; sign binaries per enterprise policy.

### DWG FastView markup
- **Tags**: terms 2d
- **Definition**: Lightweight review layer for redlines and measures in viewer clients—separate from full DWG editing.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Clarify whether markups round‑trip to desktop CAD or stay as overlays.

### Large‑assembly view
- **Tags**: terms 3d mfg
- **Definition**: Navigation modes for heavy 3D models—levels of detail, selection filters, clipping.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Tune hardware vs software rendering; viewer apps often trade precision for FPS.

### IFC interchange
- **Tags**: terms aec beginner
- **Definition**: Open BIM schema for exchanging building models among tools—LOD, MVD drive what travels cleanly.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Coordinate with partners on authoring vs coordination exports.

### DWG Compare
- **Tags**: terms beginner 2d gstarcad
- **Definition**: A core 2026 feature that identifies differences between two versions of a drawing with color‑coded overlays.
- **Context & Best Practice**: In GstarCAD 2026, comparison logic is optimized for faster diffing of complex Xrefs.

### Parametric Constraints
- **Tags**: terms 3d gstarcad
- **Definition**: Rules that define geometry relationships (Parallel, Tangent) and dimensions (Distance, Radius) linked to variables.
- **Context & Best Practice**: GstarCAD 2026 Phase 2 introduces the Parameters Manager for formula‑driven design.

### Dynamic Input
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: Provides a command interface near the cursor to help keep focus on the drafting area.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Press F12 to toggle on and off.
- **URL**: https://gstarcademy.com/kb/concepts/dynamic-input

### Annotative Scaling
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: Automatically sizes text, dimensions, and blocks based on viewport scale.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Eliminates the need for multiple text layers.

### Sheet Set Manager
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: Organizes, displays, and manages sheet layouts across multiple drawing files.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Crucial for large project coordination.
- **URL**: https://gstarcademy.com/kb/concepts/sheet-set-manager

### Paper Space
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: The layout environment used for creating title blocks and plot sheets.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Contrasts with Model Space where 1:1 drawing occurs.

### Object Snap (OSNAP)
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: Forces the cursor to snap to exact points like endpoints, midpoints, and centers.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Essential for drafting precision.

### Hatch
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: Fills an enclosed area or selected objects with a pattern, solid fill, or gradient.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Often used to represent materials in sections.

### Polyline
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: A connected sequence of line and arc segments treated as a single object.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Can have width and thickness assigned.

### AutoLISP
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: A programming language used inside AutoCAD to automate repetitive commands.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Not supported in AutoCAD LT.
- **URL**: https://gstarcademy.com/kb/concepts/autolisp

### Viewport
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: A 'window' on a layout sheet that looks into model space at a specific scale.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Can be polygonal or locked to prevent accidental zoom.

### External Reference (XREF)
- **Tags**: terms autocad
- **Definition**: A master drawing that links in other DWG files without embedding them.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Keeps file sizes low and enables team drafting.

### Revit Family
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: A parametric component library file (.rfa) that can be loaded into a project.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Includes system, loadable, and in-place families.

### Worksharing
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: Allows multiple team members to work on the same Revit project simultaneously.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Relies on a Central Model and Local Copies.

### Workset
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: A collection of elements in a workshared project, typically divided by system or floor.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Used to control visibility and check-out rights.

### View Template
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: A collection of view properties (scale, discipline, overrides) to enforce standards.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Applying it locks the properties for consistency.

### Shared Parameter
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: A definition stored in an external text file so schedules and tags can read the data across projects.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Critical for cross-family data aggregation.

### Level
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: An infinite horizontal plane that acts as a reference for floor, roof, and ceiling hosts.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Usually represents finished floor elevations.

### Phasing
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: Tracks the lifecycle of elements across time (Existing, Demolished, New Construction).
- **Context & Best Practice**: Automatically generates proper graphical overrides.

### Schedule
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: A tabular display of information extracted directly from the properties of project elements.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Updating the schedule updates the 3D model bidirectionally.

### System Family
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: Families built into the Revit template (walls, roofs, floors) that cannot be saved externally.
- **Context & Best Practice**: You duplicate types to create variations.

### Design Options
- **Tags**: terms revit
- **Definition**: Allows exploring multiple alternative designs within a single project file.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Keeps the main model clean while alternatives are reviewed.

### IPT (Part)
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: The foundational 3D modeling file format in Inventor for single components.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Can represent solid bodies or sheet metal parts.

### IAM (Assembly)
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: A file that constraints multiple IPT parts together to simulate real-world mechanisms.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Contains BOM and motion data.

### IPN (Presentation)
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: Used to create exploded views, animations, and assembly instructions.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Feeds directly into 2D drawing views.

### iLogic
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: An integrated VB.NET environment to automate rules and drive parametric configurations.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Accessible to non-programmers via snippet insertion.

### Content Center
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: A database of millions of standard components (fasteners, steel profiles).
- **Context & Best Practice**: Connects with Vault to manage standard libraries.

### Model States
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: Allows multiple representations of a part or assembly in one file (e.g., machined vs cast).
- **Context & Best Practice**: Replaces legacy Levels of Detail (LODs).

### Frame Generator
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: Automates the creation of structural steel frames along sketch wireframes.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Handles miters, notches, and end caps automatically.

### AnyCAD
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: Technology allowing Inventor to link third-party CAD files without translation.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Retains associativity if the native file updates.

### Sheet Metal Rules
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: Global definitions controlling material thickness, bend radius, and relief shape.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Drives flat pattern generation accuracy.

### Shrinkwrap
- **Tags**: terms inventor
- **Definition**: Creates a simplified outer shell of a complex assembly to protect IP and save memory.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Useful for sharing models with external vendors.

### Body vs Component
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: A body is a single solid; a component is a container holding bodies, sketches, and origins.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Always create components to enable joint motion.

### Parametric Timeline
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: Records design history at the bottom of the screen; can be rewound to edit past features.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Forms the basis of parametric modeling in Fusion.

### Joint
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: Defines motion degrees of freedom between components (e.g., slider, revolute, rigid).
- **Context & Best Practice**: Replaces traditional multi-step mating constraints.

### T-Splines
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: The technology powering the Form workspace for sub-divisional, organic surface modeling.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Great for ergonomic industrial design.

### Generative Design
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: Uses cloud computing and AI to synthesize hundreds of structural design options.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Optimized for weight, strength, and manufacturing method.

### CAM Setup
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: Defines stock size, origin point, and machine type in the Manufacturing workspace.
- **Context & Best Practice**: The prerequisite for generating toolpaths.

### Cloud Rendering
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: Offloads complex ray-tracing calculations to Autodesk's servers, freeing local hardware.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Consumes cloud credits based on quality.

### Direct Modeling
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: A history-free mode allowing push/pull changes to geometry without a timeline.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Perfect for modifying imported, dumb solids.

### Mesh Workspace
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: Tools to repair, remesh, and convert STL/OBJ faceted files into usable solid bodies.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Essential for reverse engineering 3D scans.

### Fusion Team Hub
- **Tags**: terms fusion
- **Definition**: The cloud storage environment where projects, files, and role-based permissions reside.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Enables cross-organization collaboration.

### TIN Surface
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: A Triangulated Irregular Network representing topographical ground data.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Can represent existing ground (EG) or finished ground (FG).

### Alignment
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: A 2D geometric path defining the horizontal routing of a road, pipe, or channel.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Stationing is generated along this baseline.

### Profile
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: Represents the vertical elevation changes along an Alignment path.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Displayed in a Profile View grid.

### Assembly
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: The cross-section template of a corridor, built from individual subassemblies like lanes and curbs.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Acts as the 'extrusion profile' for roads.

### Corridor
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: The complex 3D model generated by combining an Alignment, Profile, and Assembly.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Produces material volume calculations.

### Feature Line
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: A smart 3D line storing varied elevations at vertices, heavily used in site grading.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Can interact to create dynamic surfaces.

### Grading Group
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: A collection of grading objects (like pond slopes) that interact to generate a unified surface.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Automatically balances cut and fill.

### Pipe Network
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: Intelligent objects representing gravity or pressure piping systems with structures.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Includes clash detection against other utilities.

### Data Shortcuts
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: XML links allowing civil objects (surfaces, alignments) to be referenced across multiple DWGs.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Replaces Xrefs for intelligent civil data.

### Parcel
- **Tags**: terms civil3d
- **Definition**: An enclosed polygon representing property boundaries, automatically tracking area and perimeter.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Labels update dynamically if boundaries shift.

### NWC (Cache)
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: A lightweight exported file from native authoring tools (like Revit or AutoCAD).
- **Context & Best Practice**: Loads significantly faster than native geometry.

### NWF (File Set)
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: The working federated master file linking multiple NWC files together without embedding them.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Holds clashes, viewpoints, and markups.

### NWD (Document)
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: A baked, single-file snapshot containing all geometry and markups, heavily compressed.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Used to share frozen project states with clients.

### Clash Detective
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: Module to find interferences between structural, architectural, and MEP disciplines.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Only available in Navisworks Manage.

### TimeLiner
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: Connects 3D model elements to project schedules to visualize construction sequencing.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Often called 4D BIM.

### Quantification
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: Extracts highly accurate bill of materials, areas, and volumes mapped to cost codes.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Often called 5D BIM.

### Search Set
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: A dynamic grouping of elements based on property logic (e.g., 'Category = Duct').
- **Context & Best Practice**: Updates automatically if new elements match.

### Selection Set
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: A static grouping of manually picked items, saved for quick isolation or coloring.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Does not update if the model changes.

### Viewpoint
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: A saved camera view retaining section boxes, hiding overrides, and redlines.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Crucial for generating clash reports.

### SwitchBack
- **Tags**: terms navisworks
- **Definition**: A tool that syncs the Navisworks camera view directly back to the native Revit/CAD application.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Speeds up error correction.

### FeatureManager
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: The design tree on the left of the screen listing chronological modeling steps.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Equivalent to the browser in other CAD systems.

### Configuration
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: Creates multiple variations of a part within a single document.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Driven by a Design Table.

### SmartMates
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: Automatically applies mating constraints by holding 'Alt' and dragging faces together.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Dramatically speeds up assembly.

### Pack and Go
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: Gathers all related files for a model design into a folder or zip file.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Prevents missing references when sharing.

### Weldments
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: A multi-body part environment for designing frames from standard structural profiles.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Automatically generates cut lists.

### Mate Reference
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: Pre-defines mating rules on a part so it snaps instantly when dropped into assemblies.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Great for standard hardware.

### SpeedPak
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: Creates a simplified configuration of an assembly without losing references.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Increases performance on large assemblies.

### Evaluate Tab
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: Contains tools for mass properties, measuring, interference detection, and draft analysis.
- **Context & Best Practice**: The diagnostic hub of the interface.

### SOLIDWORKS PDM
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: Product Data Management software managing file versions and check-in/out workflows.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Integrates directly into Windows Explorer.
- **URL**: https://gstarcademy.com/kb/concepts/solidworks-pdm

### SLDDRW
- **Tags**: terms solidworks
- **Definition**: The 2D drawing file format dynamically linked to the 3D part or assembly.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Updates automatically if the 3D model changes.

### GSD (Generative Shape Design)
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: The premier workbench for complex surface modeling and wireframe skeletons.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Industry standard in automotive Class-A surfacing.

### PartBody
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: The primary container within a CATPart holding solid mechanical features.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Can interact with surfaces via boolean operations.

### Geometrical Set
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: A container for wireframes and surfaces, organized independently from the solid history tree.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Keeps construction elements organized.

### PowerCopy
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: A smart template capturing geometry and design intent that can be rapidly instantiated.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Adapts to new target surfaces.

### Publication
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: A method to publish important geometry (planes, sketches) to safely link between external files.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Prevents broken links when replacing parts.

### DMU (Digital Mock-Up)
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: Workbenches dedicated to reviewing massive assemblies, kinematics, and space analysis.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Handles gigabytes of visualization data.

### Knowledge Advisor
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: Embeds engineering rules, checks, and formulas directly into the design.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Turns geometry into smart, constraint-driven models.

### CGR File
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: CATIA Graphical Representation; a lightweight faceted format for visualization only.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Cannot be edited or measured precisely.

### CAA (Component Application Architecture)
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: The C++ API framework for developing deep, custom workbenches in CATIA.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Used by aerospace firms for proprietary tools.

### Boolean Operations
- **Tags**: terms catia
- **Definition**: Combining multiple PartBodies using Add, Remove, or Intersect logic.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Essential for complex mold and die design.
- **URL**: https://gstarcademy.com/kb/concepts/boolean-operations

### Pro/ENGINEER
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: The legacy brand name of Creo, pioneering the parametric, feature-based modeling paradigm.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Renamed to Creo in 2010.

### Creo Direct
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: A standalone app or mode for history-free, direct modeling interactions.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Ideal for late-stage design changes.

### Family Table
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: A spreadsheet driving multiple instances of a part (e.g., varying lengths of a screw).
- **Context & Best Practice**: Similar to configurations in other tools.

### Windchill
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: PTC's enterprise PLM software tightly integrated with Creo for data management.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Manages workflows, BOMs, and CAD versions.

### Unite Technology
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: Allows Creo to directly open non-native CAD formats without translation errors.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Preserves design intent from CATIA, NX, etc.

### Mapkey
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: A recorded keyboard macro that automates repetitive GUI clicks in Creo.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Massively improves user drafting speed.

### Skeleton Model
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: A special part used in Top-Down design to distribute spatial claims to sub-components.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Does not appear in the final BOM.

### FMX (Flexible Modeling)
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: Allows geometry editing directly on the model while retaining parametric intelligence.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Blends direct and parametric paradigms.

### Mechanism Dynamics
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: Evaluates the kinematic and dynamic performance of moving assemblies.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Includes motors, springs, and gravity simulations.

### ModelCHECK
- **Tags**: terms creo
- **Definition**: An automated tool that evaluates CAD models against corporate modeling standards.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Prevents bad geometry from entering the vault.

### Standard Parts Library
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: A massive built-in library of screws, nuts, and pins that conform to global standards.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Automatically sizes based on hole selections.

### Automatic BOM
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: Scans balloons and parts references to generate an associative bill of materials table.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Updates immediately if balloons are deleted.

### Intelligent Dimension
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: A single dimensioning tool that adapts to lines, arcs, or angles depending on cursor position.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Replaces multiple distinct dimension commands.

### Hole Chart
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: Automatically detects hole diameters and locations, generating a coordinate table.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Crucial for CNC drilling preparation.

### Hidden Line Evaluation
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: Automatically calculates foreground/background overlaps in 2D to dash hidden edges.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Saves hours of manual layer adjustments.

### Title Block Automation
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: Title blocks dynamically link to project properties and automatically scale to the layout.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Ensures ISO/ANSI compliance.

### Power Erase
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: Deleting a mechanical feature automatically heals the surrounding geometry.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Example: Erasing a screw hole restores the solid plate line.

### Detail View Generator
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: Draw a circle around an area to instantly generate a scaled, associative detail callout.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Updates if the source geometry changes.

### Surface Texture Symbol
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: Pre-configured symbols for machining finishes adhering to international standards.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Attaches parametrically to target lines.

### Welding Symbol
- **Tags**: terms gstarcad-mech
- **Definition**: A dialogue-driven tool to generate complex welding instructions on the drawing.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Supports all weld types and staggers.

### My Cloud
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: The integrated storage allowing automatic file synchronization across mobile and PC.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Provides a seamless transition from office to site.

### Offline Mode
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Allows caching of heavy DWGs to local device storage for construction site review.
- **Context & Best Practice**: No internet required to view or markup.

### Inquiry Tools
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Snap-based tools to accurately measure distance, area, and coordinates without editing.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Ensures site dimensions match plans.

### Markup
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Add clouds, text notes, and voice memos to drawings for rapid communication.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Syncs back to the office instantly.

### Font Manager
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Handles missing SHX fonts by allowing users to map substitutions or upload missing files.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Prevents garbled text on mobile displays.

### Layer Control
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Toggle visibility, freeze, and lock layers directly from the mobile interface.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Helps isolate specific disciplines like MEP.

### Layout Switching
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Navigate between Model space and multiple Paper Space layouts effortlessly.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Retains viewport scaling settings.

### Export to PDF
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Convert a DWG view into a high-quality PDF directly from the mobile app.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Great for emailing clients.

### Extract Text
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Scans the drawing to pull all text entities into an exportable list or table.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Useful for verifying bill of materials.

### Version Compare
- **Tags**: terms fastview
- **Definition**: Overlays two iterations of a drawing, highlighting additions in green and deletions in red.
- **Context & Best Practice**: Crucial for change order verification.
